title: Generic Queue Data Structure
story: A print spooler processes jobs in order: first submitted, first printed. A customer service line works the same way. You need a Queue - but one that works for print jobs, customers, or anything else. Generic Queue[T] to the rescue.
why: Queue[T] demonstrates first-in-first-out (FIFO) behavior with a generic implementation that works for any data type.
analogy: A ticket line at a movie theater: the first person in line gets the first ticket. You join at the back (enqueue) and leave from the front (dequeue). That's FIFO - exactly what a Queue guarantees.
try_it: Simulate a help desk: create Queue[Str] with three customer names, then process them in a while loop: `while !q.is_empty() { serve next customer }`. Print 'Serving: <name>' for each.
tips: enqueue adds to the back (end of Vec)
dequeue removes from the front (index 0) and shifts everything left
FIFO = First In, First Out — the opposite of a Stack's LIFO
common_mistakes: Dequeuing from the wrong end — must be index 0, not the last element
Forgetting to handle empty queue — return Option.None
Using dequeue when you meant front (which should NOT remove the item)
